question: When did Larsen & Toubro (L&T) launch the Indian Navy’s Second Multi-Purpose Vessel (MPV)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**January 2025**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Larsen & Toubro (L&T)** achieved a significant milestone by launching the **second Multi-Purpose Vessel (MPV)** for the **Indian Navy** on **January 16, 2025**.
 
• The vessel, named **‘Samarthak’**, was launched at **L&T’s Kattupalli Shipyard** located near **Chennai**, **Tamil Nadu**.
 
• The launch ceremony was graced by **Smt. Tanvi Singh**, who performed the traditional honors, in the presence of **Vice Admiral Krishna Swaminathan**, the **Vice Chief of Naval Staff**.
 
• This vessel is the second in a series of **two MPVs** being constructed by **L&T** under a contract signed with the **Ministry of Defence** in **March 2022**.
 
• The first vessel of this class, named **‘Vayan’**, was launched earlier in **September 2024**, demonstrating the rapid pace of construction at the shipyard.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Vessel Role and Capabilities:**
 
 
• The **Multi-Purpose Vessels (MPVs)** are designed to perform a wide array of roles including **maritime surveillance**, **towing of targets**, and acting as a platform for **naval training**.
 
• They are also equipped to provide **Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR)**, making them vital assets for non-combat maritime operations.
 
• The ships feature advanced **indigenous equipment** and systems, aligning with the **‘Aatmanirbhar Bharat’** (Self-reliant India) initiative.
 
 
 
• **Technical Specifications:**
 
 
• The vessels are approximately **106 meters** in length and **15 meters** in width.
 
• They are capable of reaching a maximum speed of **15 knots** and have an endurance suited for prolonged deployments in the **Indian Ocean Region (IOR)**.
 
• The contract for these **two vessels** was valued at approximately **Rs. 887 crore**.
 
 
 
• **L&T Shipbuilding:**
 
 
• **L&T** is a major private player in **India's defense manufacturing** sector, specifically in naval shipbuilding.
 
• The **Kattupalli Shipyard** is a state-of-the-art facility that has delivered several **Interceptor Boats**, **Offshore Patrol Vessels (OPVs)**, and **Floating Docks** to the **Indian Navy** and **Indian Coast Guard**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Strategic Significance:** The induction of **MPVs** like **Samarthak** will allow the **Indian Navy** to phase out aging auxiliary ships and enhance its auxiliary fleet's operational efficiency.
 
• **Launch vs Commissioning:** While the **launch** occurred in **January 2025**, the vessel will now undergo a series of **sea trials** and equipment fit-outs before being formally **commissioned** into active service.
 
• **Timeline:** The delivery of both vessels is planned to be completed within a **36-month** window from the start of the project, highlighting the efficiency of **indigenous private shipyards**.
